pages.text: OreSpawn's monsters drop some of the best materials in the pack, and it would be rude not to wear them. This chapter has two projects: a venom band cut from Emperor Scorpion chitin, and vest plating pressed from Mobzilla's own scales.$(p)Both follow the same plan: kill something enormous and keep the pieces.

pages.title: Emperor's Chitin Band
pages.text: An 8% drop from Emperor Scorpions killed by a player. The $(l:orespawn_integrations:bestiary/emperor_scorpion)donor$() is the size of a house, so come ready. It goes in the Artifacts hands slot, and Curios and Accessories slots accept it too.
The patient alternative: six Emperor Scorpion Scales, two gold ingots, one spider eye. Same band, no gambling.

pages.title: The Venom
pages.text: While worn, every melee hit poisons the target: Poison II for 4 seconds, on a 5-second cooldown. Venom particles show when it triggers and the tooltip spells it out. Getting a band earns Venom Wristwear.$(p)Short on scorpions? Desert tombs have plenty. Cracking the pharaoh's hoard can wake an Emperor Scorpion on the spot. See $(l:orespawn_integrations:living_world/structure_treasures)Structure Treasures$().

pages.title: Mobzilla Plating
pages.text: Four Godzilla Scales, compass points around a Twilight Forest Traveller's Vest. The grid does the riveting.

pages.title: The Plating
pages.text: The plated vest gains +4 Armor and +0.3 knockback resistance, with tooltip lines to prove it; a grindstone strips the plating whenever you want the featherweight back. Rounding up vest and scales earns Wearing the Boss.$(p)$(l:orespawn_integrations:bosses/mobzilla)Mobzilla$() took the hit so you don't have to. Repeatedly. That is the entire theory of armor.
